deletion_policy.description:
Whether Terraform will be prevented from destroying the instance. Defaults to "DELETE".
When a 'terraform destroy' or 'terraform apply' would delete the instance,
the command will fail if this field is set to "PREVENT" in Terraform state.
When set to "ABANDON", the command will remove the resource from Terraform
management without updating or deleting the resource in the API.
When set to "DELETE", deleting the resource is allowed.

description.rationale: Description is metadata only and does not affect any security controls.

location.description: The location of the resource. The only supported location is global so far.
location.rationale: Determines the region/zone where the resource is created. Policy should restrict it to an approved-region whitelist for data residency; the allowed set is parameterised (a hardcoded example whitelist is acceptable).

name.description: The resource name of the log scope. For example: \'projects/my-project/locations/global/logScopes/my-log-scope\'
name.rationale: The log scope name is a unique identifier for the resource. It has no direct security implications beyond being a reference name.

parent.rationale: Parent identifies the resource hierarchy location. Has no direct security impact on the log scope.

resource_names.description: Names of one or more parent resources : *  \'projects/[PROJECT_ID]\' May alternatively be one or more views : * \'projects/[PROJECT_ID]/locations/[LOCATION_ID]/buckets/[BUCKET_ID]/views/[VIEW_ID]\' A log scope can include a maximum of 50 projects and a maximum of 100 resources in total.
resource_names.rationale: Lists the parent projects/views included in this log scope. These are references to other resources, and a generic policy could only constrain the set by hardcoding specific project/view names, which is overreaching; actual access to the scoped logs is governed by IAM on the views, not by this membership list.
